analysis:
The only change in docs/architecture/inference.md is one added row at head line 1406 in the scheduler configuration table. It documents `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens`, an effective-token floor for the paged complete checkpoint store on dense Qwen3.5/3.8. With the floor, a prefill range ends just below the prompt end when that saves at least the floor. The row points to `EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift` and the prefix-cache.md section on streamed complete checkpoints. I examined the two base_text units (lines 806-1215 and 1216-1611), which are unchanged context. Nothing in them is edited, and they sit outside the changed range.

This is documentation only. It adds no code, endpoint, key handling, or wire-protocol change, so I found no security regression. Possible relevance is to T-041, the prefix-cache cross-tenant and TTFT oracle and at-rest cache surface. The row describes a scheduler checkpoint-boundary policy that may change which prefixes get donated to the encrypted SSD complete store. Per T-041's detection_hint, loosening the per-donation gate could widen the at-rest surface, but the docs do not show a change to the adoption bound, benefit floor, TTL, HMAC naming, cacheSalt scoping, or AAD. Whether the underlying source (not in this batch) changes donation eligibility is unverified. If it does, it should be checked against the T-041 per-donation gate, salt scoping, and the SEC-035 sign-off. Media requests are already excluded from prefix capture per the unchanged text. The implementing code was not supplied, so this is a coverage limit and not evidence of safety. No finding is warranted from the docs change alone.
